image_description: Three baseballs are displayed inside individual transparent compartments of a metal rack or case. The leftmost ball has blue text/logos, the middle one has red stitching and a blue logo, and the rightmost shows partial red stitching. The setting appears to be an industrial or storage environment with metallic structures and dim lighting.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All three visible objects are clearly spherical and proportionally consistent with standard baseball size relative to the rack compartments.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Perfectly round with uniform surface texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leftmost ball exhibits non-uniform texture due to large blue printed graphics; the middle and right balls show typical leather grain but are partially obscured or distorted by reflections/refractions through plastic covers.
All balls have white base coloring consistent with leather/synthetic material, though surface sheen varies due to lighting and protective casing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cover consists of two figure-eight-shaped pieces stitched together.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While red stitching is visible on middle and right balls, the full figure-eight seam pattern is not fully discernible due to angle, occlusion by case walls, and image resolution. Left ball lacks visible red stitching entirely.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Raised red thread forming distinctive curved seam pattern with numerous double stitches.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Middle and right balls show segments of red stitching, but 'numerous double stitches' cannot be confirmed visually — stitch count and detail are lost in compression/reflection. Left ball has no red stitching at all.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Red stitching provides high contrast against white background.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only applicable to middle/right balls; even there, contrast is reduced by glare, plastic casing distortion, and low-light conditions. Left ball fails this checkpoint entirely.
Surface reflectivity suggests glossiness, especially under overhead light source; however, some areas appear matte due to printing (left ball) or shadowing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Firm but slightly compressible feel from cork and rubber core wrapped in yarn.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tactile properties cannot be assessed visually; internal structure is invisible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White cover with red stitching is traditional appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Left ball deviates significantly from traditional appearance due to dominant blue graphics replacing red stitching. Middle/right balls partially conform but lack complete traditional seam visibility.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Large blue printed logo/text disrupts expected uniform leather texture; while not physically impossible (custom-printed balls exist), it violates taxonomy’s ‘traditional’ expectation and may indicate AI over-generation of branding elements.

artifact_observations.location: Plastic case walls around middle and right balls
artifact_observations.reasoning: Refraction and warping effects along vertical dividers suggest slight geometric inconsistency between object boundaries and container geometry — common in AI renders where transparency/reflection physics are approximated.

artifact_observations.location: Background metallic framework and floor grating
artifact_observations.reasoning: Non-uniform blur gradient across background elements suggests depth-of-field simulation rather than optical lens behavior; edges soften inconsistently without clear focal plane logic.

Text appears as stylized letterforms ('HAR', '60') but lacks legibility or coherent brand identity; characters merge into abstract shapes upon close inspection — classic AI artifact when generating logos/text on curved surfaces.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that generated objects belong to correct ImageNet class despite visual deviations (e.g., blue graphics). Must confirm semantic alignment before structural audit.
Audit whether transparent barriers maintain topological continuity with frame structure; detect edge bleeding or floating panels caused by refraction errors.
Holistic assessment of lighting coherence, shadow consistency, and micro-texture fidelity across all components — critical for detecting subtle generative artifacts missed by targeted audits.
Extract and validate character-level integrity of printed text/logo; determine if gibberish stems from OCR failure vs. intentional design vs. AI hallucination.

focus_areas: Stitching completeness and anatomical accuracy on middle/right baseballs
Texture uniformity vs. printed graphic intrusion on left baseball
Geometric plausibility of transparent case walls and their interaction with contained spheres
Legibility and structural validity of blue text/logos on left ball
Lighting directionality and reflection consistency across multiple reflective surfaces
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Prioritize evidence from fine_grained_classifier regarding class membership despite aesthetic deviations. Treat text_gibberish severity as potentially underestimated if characters dissolve into noise at higher magnification. Consider whether perspective_distortion in case walls indicates deeper spatial grounding failure beyond local warping. Do not assume tactile checkpoints can be validated visually — mark untestable unless indirect cues (deformation under pressure) are present.
